title: LibRPA IBZ->BZ restore lost the atom-swap block ordering: Si density fails at 6 points and 10 raw GW bands are NaN while 30/30 symmetry unit tests pass
symptom: With current master_ghj LibRPA, a real Si 64-point density check failed at 6 points and raw `GW_band_spin_1.dat` contained 10 NaN in bands 43-44. A newly added Si material regression detects about 1.39 eV of error from the old program. The pre-existing 30-test symmetry suite was 30/30 green, and the 'full BZ, symmetry off' GW reference gave a plausible gap (~1.028 eV).
root_cause: Commit 367548d3 (Aug 23) changed the atom-mapping direction of the density restore: src/core/symmetry_context.cpp (IBZ->BZ atom index and Bloch phase ownership; the atom blocks of the full wavefunction rotation matrix and its derivatives were not swapped together) together with the corresponding MPI restore of requested source atom pairs in src/core/meanfield_mpi.cpp. The regression suite had no case with an atom-exchanging symmetry operation: the Si material cases ran with LibRPA symmetry OFF, the symmetry-enabled BN/LiH/MgO cases have operations that do not exchange atom positions, and the bcc-He primitive cell has a single atom. The unit test `test_dense_kspace_rotation_matrix_orders_atom_swap_blocks` had two expected values edited to pass. ABACUS's own symmetry output was correct - the defect is in LibRPA's equivalent-atom mapping and phase restoration.
minimal_fix: Restore the atom-swap block ordering: swap the atom blocks in the wavefunction rotation matrix and adjust the derivatives in src/core/symmetry_context.cpp, and adjust the MPI restore of requested source atom pairs in src/core/meanfield_mpi.cpp, keeping the original unit-test expectations untouched. Commit `e0407be4` (branch codex/si-kstar-atom-route-fix, merged into master_ghj), plus regression hardening `d38161e3` that requires the log to show the three symmetry switches ON, compares all 18 states against an independent full-k reference, and rejects non-finite values.
validation: 30 symmetry unit tests + the real Si 64-point density check over all three restore paths (block, full matrix, wavefunction; max relative error ~2.38e-5; the unpatched master still errors on the same data), serial and 4-process MPI. Then symmetry=1 + shrink + reader-v1 Si k444 GW: PBE gap 0.54301 eV, GW gap 1.02789 eV, 1 MPI and 4 MPI identical to output precision (17:36 and 14:53), versus the full-k reference GW energies within 0.17 meV (gap difference 0.01 meV) and the Gamma valence triplet degeneracy recovered; 24 material regressions pass.
avoid: Do not conclude 'symmetry is fine' because the regression suite is green - first check whether any covered case contains an atom-exchanging operation. Do not relax the band comparator: it previously accepted NaN on both sides and hid the anomaly. Also do not weaken the new Si reference to make the number pass.
